category: crypto market data API (assets, exchanges, markets, rates, indicators)

free_tier.stated: Free tier: 500 credits per month at 5 API calls per minute, with no WebSocket access; each call costs 1 credit plus 1 more per 2,500 bytes of response
free_tier.notes: Every call needs an API key, also on the Free tier; the old keyless v2 host is not the current API. Responses to identical requests may come from a 60-second cache and are billed like fresh ones. Ten agent-friendly endpoints can instead be paid per call in USDC with no account. Paid tiers start at Builder, 50,000 credits per month at 30 calls per minute.

per_object_cap.stated: 100 results per page by default, up to 2,000 per page on request

retention.notes: History reaches back to July 2010 for Bitcoin; depth varies by asset.

egress.terms: not metered in bytes, but each 2,500 bytes of a response costs 1 extra credit against the 500-credit monthly allowance

interface_detail: GET https://rest.coincap.io/v3/... with Authorization: Bearer KEY or the apiKey query parameter; an MCP endpoint and WebSocket (paid tiers) also exist
tooling: curl or any HTTP client; an OpenAPI 3.0 spec is published
chaining: Spot prices and history for a few hundred calls a month; CoinPaprika and CoinLore cover the same ground with no key.

limits.value: 5 API calls per minute on the Free tier
500 credits per month on the Free tier, 1 credit per call plus 1 per 2,500 bytes

limits_note: Bulk path: none; pages of up to 2,000 rows. Storage terms: not read (unverified: the terms page captured answered HTTP 404).
binding_note: 500 credits a month, spent at 1 credit or more per call, run out long before the 5 calls per minute matter.

identity_cost.detail: A key needs an account made at coincap.io; the vendor says no credit card is required. The fields of the sign-up form were not read, so email as the only identifier is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: A call with no key answers HTTP 401; the Free tier is capped at 5 calls per minute.
confidence_note: Tier numbers are read from the vendor docs and pricing page; a keyless call answered 401. The key was not exercised.
